theme: The shape of a normal day: tea, the crossword, the garden. Noticing that the shape held is enough; it does not require interrupting it to ask.

posts.text: My mother's day has a shape. Tea, the crossword, the garden if it isn't raining. I used to think I had to call to know it held. Now I think noticing it held is enough.
posts.alt: Three-panel comic strip: an adult son wonders from his kitchen counter whether his mother's morning held its shape, she waters her garden in gardening gloves with her iPhone in her cardigan pocket, and he looks at his phone's blank lit screen, relaxed. Caption: Same shape as most days.

posts.title: Three quiet signs a parent's normal day already happened
posts.text:
Three quiet signs a parent's normal day already happened

A cup made and put away. A book picked back up. A garden tended in the evening light. None of these need a phone call to notice, and none of them are proof of anything big. They are just what a normal day looks like from the outside.

posts.title: The shape, not the report

script.say: My check-ins with my parents got tactical. How are you. How's work. Okay, talk soon.
script.broll: Founder face to camera, kitchen counter behind him.

script.say: I did not want to watch my mother's day, tap by tap. I wanted to know the shape held: tea, the crossword, the garden.

script.say: Kettle notices when Mom's normal morning happens, on the phone she already carries, and tells our family in a short note, twice a day.

script.say: The shape still holds most days. That's the whole thing I wanted to know.
